subject: Design: tenant-level retention + regional storage — roadmap ask
messages:
From: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: privacy@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant retention and per-region storage options

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks again for the demo last week. A couple of quick, concrete asks from our security/privacy team as we evaluate Redwood for our clinical note ingestion pipeline: 

1) We need per-tenant configurable retention windows (e.g., 30/90/365 days) that are enforced server-side and surfaced in the admin API so our SOC team can audit settings.
2) For EU/US residency requirements, we want the ability to pin a tenant's data to a regionally isolated storage tier (not just routing) and ensure erase actions are scoped to that region.
3) Proof points: examples of how you handle cross-region failover without replicating PII, and whether an erase request removes both hot and cold copies (we have auditors who will ask).

I've attached our questionnaire (acme-gdpr-questions.pdf) and a sample retention matrix we use internally. Can you confirm whether these are on the roadmap and, if so, an approximate timeline and what the operational model looks like (self-serve vs managed migration)?

Best,
Jill Turner
Head of Privacy, Acme Health

Attachments: acme-gdpr-questions.pdf (PDF), sample-dataset.csv (CSV)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant retention and per-region storage options

Hi Jill —

Thanks for the clear asks and the attachments — very helpful. Short answers up front: yes, we are working toward tenant-level retention controls and regional storage pinning, but there are some trade-offs and implementation details to align on (see below).

I'm looping in Karthik (infra/runtime) and Marissa (product) to capture technical constraints and product commitments. Proposed next steps:

- We’ll run a 60-minute technical workshop next week to walk through your retention matrix and map it to Redwood's model. Please share a couple of preferred times.
- Karthik, can you prepare a short tech note on the current behavior for cross-region failover and what it would take to make per-tenant region pinning (no replication) a first-class capability?
- Marissa, can you sketch an admin API surface that exposes retention TTL and storage-region for a tenant and call out what would be self-serve vs managed?

I attached an internal retention-matrix-v2.xlsx that highlights the axes we typically need from customers (legal hold, soft-delete vs hard-delete, archive windows).

Jill — is your primary requirement enforcement (server-side guardrail) or visibility + controls for your operators? If enforcement is required, we'll need to align on SLA for on-demand erasures.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention-matrix-v2.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant retention and per-region storage options

On Tue, 2026-09-07 at 11:03 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> I'm looping in Karthik (infra/runtime) and Marissa (product) to capture technical constraints and product commitments.

Quick tech summary we can share in the workshop:

- Current state: we support per-tenant routing (requests go to nearest region) and a logical tenant tag, but underlying persistent storage is multi-region for durability on hosted tier. Cold backups may be geo-replicated depending on storage class.

- Work required for pinning-without-replication: introduce a region-affinity storage class + owner-scoped replica policy. That involves changes across the control plane (tenant metadata), object lifecycle controller (prevent replication), and backup tooling (region-scoped snapshots). Estimate: ~3 sprints for a focused infra team + 1 sprint of upgrade verification/testing.

- Erase semantics: today our erase flow marks data for deletion and deletes hot KV/segments quickly; cold snapshots are on a retention schedule and require snapshot-expiration tooling to ensure they are removed. To meet 'erase all copies on request' we need: immediate tombstones + expedited snapshot expiration + auditable job that writes an erase manifest for the tenant. Additional ~2 sprints to implement and harden, plus a compliance review.

Questions for product:
- Do we expose a single API that accepts TTL + region (e.g., POST /v1/tenants/{id}/retention {ttl: 365, region: us-east-1, enforcement: strict})?
- Do we allow tenant owners to change region after data has been collected (migration path)?

I'll bring a short tech diagram and a list of compatibility constraints to the workshop.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Staff Engineer, Infra — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acmehealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant retention and per-region storage options — proposed roadmap sync

Hi Jill / team —

Thanks for raising this. High level product position and proposed commitment:

- Product position: We treat per-tenant retention and region pinning as enterprise capabilities. For compliance-first customers (PHI/PII), we can offer a Private/ Dedicated plan that supports region-affinity storage with enforced erasure semantics.

- Roadmap ask: propose we ship an MVP that includes:
  * Admin API for TTL + storage_region + enforcement_mode (self-serve for Dedicated; managed for Hosted until we certify)
  * Control-plane flagging to prevent cross-region replication for flagged tenants
  * Expedited erase job with audit log and erase_manifest export

- Timeline (high level): discovery + workshop (wk of Sep 14), technical spike and infra work (Oct — Nov, 2–3 sprints), beta with 1–2 customers (Dec), GA in H1 2027 (subject to compliance sign-off).

Operational asks from Acme for beta: a tenant sample dataset and a list of typical retention profiles + frequency of on-demand erasures (so we can size expedited erase infra).

Next steps: Stephanie to coordinate workshop times; Jill if you can share two 60-min slots next week I’ll lock the calendar and we’ll include a short agenda.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Redwood Inference
